newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian coffee arrivals over 300,000 T by July 4.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian coffee arrivals over 300,000 T by July 4.

text.p: Arrivals of Ivory Coast's near-record 1996/97 season (October-September) coffee crop at ports totalled just over 300,000 tonnes by July 4, compared to about 194,000 tonnes by the same date in 1995/96, port sources said on Tuesday.
"That (302,000 tonnes) figure is about right," a coffee industry source confirmed, putting weekly arrivals at about 3,500 tonnes against 1,500 for the same period last year.
The latest figures showed around 186,000 tonnes were delivered to the main port of Abidjan, with the remainder taken to San Pedro or not included in either port's total.
Ivory Coast's bumper 1996/97 crop follows a 1995/96 harvest of 180,000 tonnes and is well above an official forecast of 230,000 tonnes -- with three months of the season still to go.
A separate set of figures circulating in the market showing arrivals up to the end of May put arrivals then at 275,000 tonnes -- one third up from 182,000 by the same date in 1995/96.
Industry analysts said their records showed the 1996/97 crop was the largest since a 367,000 tonnes harvest in 1980/81.
"It is the highest coffee crop in the recent history of Ivory Coast (after 1980/81)," said one analyst.
Ivorian exporters plan to raise coffee conditioning plant capacity for 1997/98 to avoid a repeat of pre-export quality problems encountered in 1996/97.
